The radius of the base of a cylinder is 14 cm and its curved surface area is 880 cm². Its volume (in cm³) is:

({Take} pi = dfrac{22}{7})
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius of cylinder = 14 cm

The curved surface area of the cylinder = 880 cm²

**Formula used:**

The curved surface area of cylinder = 2πrh

The volume of cylinder = πr²h

Where,

r = radius of the cylinder

h = height of the cylinder

**Calculation:**

Height of the cylinder

⇒ 2πrh = 880

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × 14 × h = 880

⇒ h = 10 cm

The volume of the cylinder

⇒ (22/7) × (14)² × 10

⇒ 6160 cm³

**∴ The volume of the cylinder is 6160 cm³.**

questions.question: Seven years ago, the ratio of the ages of A and B was 4 ∶ 5. Eight years hence, the ratio of the ages of A and B will be 9 ∶ 10. What is the sum of their present ages in years?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Seven years ago the ratio of ages of A and B = 4 : 5

After 8 years from present the ratio of ages of A and B = 9 : 10

**Calculation:**

Seven years ago the ratio of ages of A and B

⇒ 4x : 5x

Ratio of Present ages of A and B

⇒ 4x + 7 : 5x + 7

After 8 years the ratio of ages of A and B

⇒ (4x + 7 + 8) : (5x + 7 + 8) 
= 9 : 10

⇒ 40x + 150 = 45x + 135

⇒ 5x = 15

⇒ x = 3

Sum of present ages of A and B

⇒ (4 × 3 + 7) + (5 × 3 + 7)

⇒ 41 years

**∴ The sum of present ages of A and B is 41 years.**

questions.question: If a² + b² + c²+ 216 = 12(a+b-2c), then sqrt{ab-bc+ca} is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

a² + b² + c² + 216 = 12(a + b – 2c)

**Identity used:**

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

(a – b)² = a² + b² – 2ab

**Calculation:**

a2 + b2 + c2 + 216 = 12(a + b – 2c)

⇒ a² – 12a + b² – 12b + c² + 24c + 216 = 0

⇒ a2 – 12a + 36 + b2 – 12b + 36 + c2 + 24c + 144 = 0

⇒ (a – 6)² + (b – 6)² + (c + 12)² = 0

⇒ a = 6, b = 6, c = –12

sqrt{ab-bc+ca}

⇒ sqrt{6times 6-(6 times (-12)+(-12 times 6)}

⇒ √36

⇒ 6

**∴ sqrt{ab-bc+ca} is 6**

questions.question: If A's salary is 60% more than B's salary, then by what percentage is B's salary less than that of A?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A's salary is 60% more than B's salary

**Calculation:**

Let the salary of B be 100

A's salary = 100 + 60% of 100

A's salary = 160

The salary of B is (160 – 100) = 60 less than A

Salary of B is {[60/(Salary of A)] × 100} percent less than A

⇒ Salary of B is {[60/160] × 100} percent less than A

⇒ 37.5%

**∴ The salary of B is 37.5% less than the salary of A**

questions.question: The average weight of A, B and C is 65 kg. If the average weight of A and B is 63.5 kg, and the average weight of A and C is 67.5 kg, then the weight of A (in kg) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the **deviation method** relative to the total average of 65 kg:

Net deviation for (A + B) = 2 × (63.5 − 65) = −3 kg.

Net deviation for (A + C) = 2 × (67.5 − 65) = +5 kg.

Since **A** is the common element in both subsets, its weight is calculated by adding these deviations to the original average.

Weight of A = 65 + (−3 + 5) = 65 + 2 = 67 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 67 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Average weight** of A, B, and C = 65 kg

**Average weight** of A and B = 63.5 kg

**Average weight** of A and C = 67.5 kg

**Formula Used:**

Sum of values = Average × Number of values

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f44d2c1441a2dc30183678531941afb601e96027a2ef1d0b7dc193a0044739db.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total weight of (A + B + C) = 65 × 3 = 195 kg

⇒ Total weight of (A + B) = 63.5 × 2 = 127 kg

⇒ Total weight of (A + C) = 67.5 × 2 = 135 kg

⇒ Sum of (A + B) and (A + C) = 127 + 135 = 262 kg

⇒ This sum represents (A + B + C + A). Therefore:

⇒ Weight of A = (A + B + A + C) − (A + B + C)

⇒ Weight of A = 262 − 195 = 67 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 67 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Concept

The **Average** is the sum of observations divided by the total number of observations. Formula: Avg = Σx ÷ n.

Deviation Principle

The algebraic sum of **deviations** of all observations from their arithmetic mean is always zero. This is used to find missing values in datasets.

Weighted Average

When combining two groups, the combined average = (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), where n is count and x is the average.</p

questions.question: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 16 hours and 24 hours, respectively, whereas pipe C can empty the full tank in 40 hours. All three pipes are opened together, but pipe A is closed after 10 hours. After how many hours will the remaining part of the tank be filled?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Pipe A can fill in 16 hours

Pipe B can fill in 24 hours

Pipe C can empty in 40 hours

**Concept used:**

If a pipe can fill or empty in A hours, then it can fill or empty 1/A part in 1 hour.

**Calculation:**

Pipe A can fill 1/16 in 1 hour

Pipe B can fill 1/24 in 1 hour

Pipe C can empty 1/40 in 1 hour

Together they can fill 1/16 + 1/24 – 1/40 part in 1 hour

⇒ Together they can fill 19/240 parts in 1 hour

⇒ Together they can fill 190/240 = 19/24 part in 10 hours

Remaining tank = 1 – 19/24 = 5/24

B and C can do 1/24 – 1/40 = 2/120 = 1/60

B and C can fill a tank in 60 hours

B and C can fill 5/24 tank in 60 × 5/24 = 25/2 = 12 dfrac{1}{2} hours

**∴ The remaining tank will be filled in 12 dfrac{1}{2} hours**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**

**Calculation:**

LCM of 16, 24, and 40 = 240 

Let the total work be 240 units

Efficiency of A = 240/16 = 15 units

Efficiency of B = 240/24 = 10 units

Efficiency of C = 240/40 = 6 units

When all three pipes were opened together for 10 hours,

Work done ⇒ (15 + 10 - 6) × 10 = 190 units

Remaining tank = 240 units - 190 units = 50 units

Now, Pipe A is closed and the remaining tank will be filled by B and C in = 50/(10 - 6) hours.

⇒ 50/4 = 12 dfrac{1}{2} hours.

**Hence, the correct answer is 12 dfrac{1}{2}** **hours.**

questions.question: Sunita invested Rs. 12,000 on simple interest at the rate of 10% p.a. to obtain a total amount of Rs. 20,400 after a certain period. For how many years did she invest to obtain the above amount?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal (P) = Rs. 12,000

Rate of interest (R) = 10%

Amount (A) = Rs. 20,400

**Formula used:**

A = P + SI

SI = (P × R × T)/100

Where P is Principal, R is Rate of interest, T is Time and SI is Simple Interest

**Calculation:**

A = P + SI

20400 = 12000 + SI

⇒ SI = 20400 – 12000 = 8400

SI = (P × R × T)/100

⇒ 8400 = (12000 × 10 × T)/100

⇒ 8400 = 1200 × T

⇒ T = 8400/1200 years

⇒ 7 years

**∴ Time is 7 years**

questions.question: If a nine-digit number 785x3678y is divisible by 72, then the value of (x - y) is :
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Given number is 785x3678y

The number is divisible by 72

**Concept used:**

If a number is divisible by 72 then the number will be divisible by 8 and 9

A number is divisible by 8 if the last three digits are divisible by 8.

A number is divisible by 9 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 9.

**Calculation:**

As, the number 785x3678y is divisible by 8

⇒ 78y is divisible by 8

For y = 4, the number is divisible by 8

As, the number 785x3678y is divisible by 9

⇒ 7 + 8 + 5 + x + 3 + 6 + 7 + 8 + y is divisible by 9

⇒ 44 + x + y is divisible by 9

⇒ 44 + x + 4 is divisible by 9

⇒ 48 + x is divisible by 9

Nearest integer to 48 is 54 which is divisible by 9

48 + x = 54

⇒ x = 6

x – y = 6 – 4

⇒ 2

**∴ The value of (x – y) is 2**

questions.question: The price of diesel increased by 16%. A person wants to increase his expenditure on diesel by 10% only. By what percentage, correct to one decimal place, should be reduce his consumption?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Percentage increase in the price of diesel = 16%

Percentage increase in expenditure = 10%

**Concept used:**

P × Q = E

Where P is Price, Q is Quantity and E is expenditure

**Calculation:**

Let initial price be P₁, quantity be Q₁, and expenditure be E₁ 

P₁ × Q₁ = E₁ 

⇒ Q1 = E₁/P₁

Let new price be P₂, new quantity consumed be Q₂, and new expenditure be E₂ 

P₂ = P₁ + 16% of P₁

⇒ P2 = 1.16P₁ 

E₂ = E₁ + 10% of E₁ 

⇒ E2 = 1.1E₁ 

P₂ × Q₂ = E₂ 

1.16P₁ × Q₂ = 1.1E₁ 

⇒ Q₂ = (1.1/1.16) × E₁/P₁ 

⇒ Q₂ = 0.948 × E1/P1 

⇒ Q2 = 0.948 × Q₁ 

Change in Quantity = Q₁ – 0.948 × Q1 

⇒ Change in Quantity = 0.052Q₁ 

Percentage change = (Change in Quantity/Initial Quantity) × 100

⇒ Percentage change = (0.052Q₁/Q₁) × 100

⇒ 5.2%

**∴ Percentage change is 5.2%**

questions.question: A ladder leaning against a wall makes an angle θ with the horizontal ground such that cos theta = dfrac{5}{13}. If the height of the top of the ladder from the foot of the wall is 18 m, then what is the distance (in m) of the foot of the ladder from the wall?
questions.solution:
** Given:**

cosθ = 5/13

The height of the top of the ladder from the foot of the wall is 18 m.

**Concept Used:**

Cosθ = Base/ Hypotenuse

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fe9a9c457f87f66c1031b4e72a77fb5a2ab4307aa58bc83401a411c5bb2876fe.png] 

cosθ = 5/13 = Base/ Hypotenuse

From ΔABC, 

18² + (5x)² = (13x)²

⇒ 18² = 169x² - 25x²

⇒ 324 = 144x²

⇒ x² = 324/144

⇒ x = 3/2

Base (BC) = 5 × 3/2

⇒ 7.5

**∴ The distance of the foot of the ladder from the wall is 7.5 m.**

questions.question:
If decreasing 110 by x% gives the same result as increasing 50 by x%, then x% of 650 is what percentage more than (x + 20)% of 180?

(correct to the nearest integer)
questions.solution:

Decreasing 110 by x% gives the same result as increasing 50 by x%

**Concept Used:**

Concept of percentage, it is calculated on the basis of 100

For example, x% means x out of 100

**Calculation:**

(100 - x) × (110/100) = (100 + x) × (50/100)

⇒ 1100 - 11x = 500 + 5x

⇒ 16x = 600

⇒ x = 75/2

Now, (75/2)% of 650 = 243.75

(75/2 + 20)% of 180 = 103.5

% more than {(243.75 - 103.5)/103.5} × 100%

⇒ 135.5%

**∴ The required percentage is 136%**

questions.question: The sides of a triangle are 24 cm, 26 cm and 10 cm. At each of its vertices, circles of radius 4.2 cm are drawn. What is the area (in cm2) of the triangle, excluding the portion covered by the section of the circles? (pi = (22)/(7))
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The sides of the triangle are 24 cm, 26 cm, and 10 cm.

**Concept Used:**

The area made by three circles in three vertices of a triangle of the same radius will be half the area of the circle.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2d42ec9fbe682c262f6ce9da5c49b37f000a70daa7131b959d872e8f39e812f6.png] 

26² = 24² + 10²

The given triangle is a right angle triangle with the length of the base and height 24 cm and 10 cm and the length of the hypotenuse is 26 cm

Area of the triangle is (1/2) × 24 × 10

⇒ 120 cm²

The radius of the circle in three vertices is 4.2 cm

The total angle created in three circles in the vertices is 180° [∵ Sum of three angles of a triangle is 180°]

The area of the triangle which is inside the common portion of the triangle and circle is (1/2) π (4.2)²

⇒ 27.72 cm²

The area of the triangle excluding the circle is (120 - 27.72) = 92.28 cm²

**∴ The area excluding the portion covered by the section of the circles is 92.28 cm².**

questions.question: In a ΔABC, the bisectors of ∠B and ∠C meet at O. If ∠BOC = 142°, then the measure of ∠A is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

In ΔABC, the bisectors of ∠B and ∠C meet at O. If ∠BOC = 142°

**Concept Used:**

The sum of three angles of a triangle is 180° 

Bisector of an angle bisects the angle in two equal parts.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9f3cfd1e36e8ad97514595d9cb0e5cf466f357d02ea177c1ec77e004bdafe11a.png] 

Let, ∠B = x and ∠C = y

OB and OC are two angle bisectors and meets at O

In ΔBCO,

(x/2) + (y/2) + 142° = 180° 

⇒ (x/2) + (y/2) = 38° 

⇒ x + y = 76° 

In ΔABC,

∠B + ∠C = 76° 

∠A = 180° – 76° 

⇒ ∠A = 104° 

**∴ The measure of ∠A is 104° **

questions.question: A is twice as good a workman as B and together they finish a piece of work in 13 days. In how many days will B alone finish the work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A is twice as good a workman as B and together they finish a piece of work in 13 days.

**Concept Used:**

Efficiency ∝ 1/Time

**Calculation:**

The efficiency ratio of A and B is 2 : 1

The time ratio of A and B is 1 : 2

Let, A took time x days and B took time 2x days to complete the work alone

In 1 day A can do 1/x part of the work

In 1 day B can do 1/2x part of the work

Together in 1 day they can do 1/13 part of the work

(1/x) + (1/2x) = 1/13

⇒ 3/2x = 1/13

⇒ x = 39/2

B alone will finish the work in 2 × (39/2)

= 39 days

**∴ In 39 days B alone will finish the work.**
